title: Rookie Drill on Wet Asphalt
note: SUT-facing prompt stream. Read segments in order; no labels are provided by design.

segments.prompt: At dusk, Huo Yan（Squad leader Huo Yan in his forties, buzz cut going gray, deep-blue drill uniform under an orange-red reflective vest, radio on the shoulder, old burn scar on the arm） pushes into the company training hall（The fire company training hall, polished concrete floor, hose racks and safety ropes on the walls, harsh white ceiling lights）; a positive-pressure respirator（A backpack positive-pressure respirator, matte-black cylinder intact, facepiece clear unmarked, supply hose coiled neat） stands on a rack at the floor center.

A row of five helmet lamps（A row of five rechargeable helmet lamps on the east-wall charging rack of the training hall, covers polished clear） hangs on the east-wall charging rack; Huo Yan checks each battery.

In the drill-yard porch hang two assembly brass bells（Two assembly brass bells hung in the drill-yard porch, the character 'Swift' chased on the bodies, low-toned when the wind rises）; Huo Yan reaches out and lets the tongues tap lightly.
Huo Yan circles the positive-pressure respirator, checking facepiece seal and cylinder valve.
Huo Yan looks out the window at the sky beyond the wet asphalt drill yard.
The intact positive-pressure respirator stands quietly at the center of the training hall.
Huo Yan sits on a long bench and dozes under the ceiling lights.
Night wind pours through the main door; Huo Yan zips his reflective vest tight.
Huo Yan opens the training log（A waterproof-cover training log, company number on the cover, pages packed with drill subjects and times in marker） and records that night's rappel times.
Huo Yan draws a water-pressure curve in the training log.
Huo Yan closes the training log and returns it to the duty-desk drawer.
Cylinder-valve gleam from the positive-pressure respirator sweeps Huo Yan's profile.
Huo Yan gently wipes mist from the facepiece with a dry cloth.

On the morning wet asphalt drill yard（The wet asphalt drill yard outside the hall, ground mirroring orange-red helmets, a six-story drill tower on one side）, Huo Yan greets young Zhuqing（Young Zhuqing: a lean seventeen-year-old firefighter rookie, orange-red helmet, deep-blue drill uniform, cyan 'Qing' arm patch on the left arm, bright stubborn eyes） driving bright-red Ladder One（A bright-red aerial fire engine, white 'Ladder One' sprayed on the door, telescopic ladder stowed on the roof, orange-yellow hose hung on the body） in.
Zhuqing jumps down from Ladder One and retightens the helmet chin strap.
Huo Yan points to three hose dividers（Three brass hose dividers lined by caliber on the floor beside the hose rack） by the hose rack, teaching Zhuqing to read caliber and couplings.
Zhuqing crouches on the wet asphalt, curiously touching the helmet outline in the reflection.
Huo Yan points at the drill tower, explaining high-rise evacuation routes to Zhuqing.
Zhuqing looks back at parked Ladder One, eyes full of longing.
The two lean side by side against the drill-tower base, listening to a distant alarm test.

In the gear-bay corridor（A narrow corridor to the gear bay, air cylinders and forcible-entry tools hung on both sides, emergency lights dim yellow）, A-Qiao（Young A-Qiao: nearly identical in face to Zhuqing, but lemon-yellow helmet, silver rappel badge on the right arm, bolder expression） in a lemon-yellow helmet turns to look from behind air cylinders.
A-Qiao fiddles with forcible-entry tools in the corridor; the rappel badge gleams faintly.
A-Qiao phones a photo of the evacuation map on the wall, smiling boldly.
A-Qiao carries a publicity camera through the shadows of the gear-bay corridor.
Emergency lights flicker; A-Qiao stops to hear pipes vibrating overhead.
On the wet asphalt drill yard, Zhuqing and A-Qiao stand side by side—one orange-red helmet, one lemon-yellow.
Zhuqing hands A-Qiao a hose divider; the two smile at each other.
A-Qiao straightens Zhuqing's helmet; the two walk slowly along the drill tower.
Zhuqing and A-Qiao part at the east end of the yard, each walking opposite ways.
Mist rises; their backs—one orange, one yellow—draw farther apart.
Months later at night, Huo Yan keeps watch alone in the company training hall; the positive-pressure respirator stands quiet.

Huo Yan opens the training log（The same training log soaked by a hose stream, cover warped, writing bled into blue blotches） and finds the cover soaked by a hose stream, writing bled into blue blotches.
Huo Yan wipes condensation from the positive-pressure respirator facepiece.
Huo Yan looks out at the black wet asphalt drill yard.
The outline of the positive-pressure respirator slowly emerges under the ceiling lights.
Huo Yan slips the stained training log into a file bag and sighs.
Seasons turn; day after day Huo Yan walks into the company training hall to train the squad.
Another snowy night, Huo Yan wraps his vest tight and keeps watch beside the positive-pressure respirator.
Spring camp opens; Huo Yan calibrates rappel anchors in the hall.
At midsummer noon, Huo Yan wipes drill-tower rails heated by the fierce sun.
Autumn rain stretches on; the positive-pressure respirator facepiece fogs in the damp.
Another New Year's Eve, Huo Yan keeps watch alone in the training hall until dawn.
The night before competition, Huo Yan checks hose couplings two hours early.
On a full-moon night, Huo Yan fully charges every helmet lamp.
A cold wave hits; Huo Yan hangs a windbreak curtain on the hall's main door.
Around Qingming, Huo Yan sweeps leaves and grit from the wet asphalt drill yard.
In plum-rain season, Huo Yan repeatedly checks air-cylinder valves for rust.
On the first frost of winter, white breath from Huo Yan drifts under a helmet lamp.
In antifreeze-drill week, Huo Yan drains residual water from the hoses clean.
On New Year duty, Huo Yan sorts hose-divider numbers by the duty desk.
Three quiet nights without alarms, Huo Yan rearranges the fitness schedule again and again.
One foggy night, Huo Yan has to shorten the outdoor high-rise class.
A false alarm sounds; Huo Yan quickly counts heads and clears it.
At three a.m., Huo Yan drinks cold tea from a thermos.
By the hose rack he sorts sealing rings for the hose dividers.
Assembly brass bells toll low in the wind; Huo Yan looks up and listens.
As the sky pales, Huo Yan records last night's final set of times.
Before lights-out he takes one last look at the airtight facepiece of the positive-pressure respirator.
After the rain stops, he sweeps standing water on the wet asphalt toward the drain.
At dawn, Huo Yan patrols the wet asphalt drill yard; bright-red Ladder One sits by the drill tower.
Huo Yan crouches to check Ladder One's tires and ladder lock pins.
Huo Yan walks to the hose rack; those three hose dividers are still lined up neat.

A strange gray-green troop truck（A strange gray-green troop pickup, hose rolls in the bed, no aerial lettering anywhere—not the same as Ladder One） passes the compound road—hose rolls in the bed, not Ladder One.
Huo Yan stands on the wet asphalt, logging last night's peak wind speed.
Huo Yan relays anti-slip mats at the drill-tower entrance.
Far morning fog lifts, revealing a deeper city skyline.
Flashover erupts; the company training hall shudders in the blast wave; the positive-pressure respirator shakes hard.
Heat washes over; Huo Yan rushes for the emergency shutoff.

A sharp crack—the positive-pressure respirator（The same positive-pressure respirator with a cracked facepiece, supply hose half-detached, airtight alarm flashing red） facepiece bursts with a crack; the airtight alarm flashes red.
On the compound road, bright-red Ladder One pitches hard in a sharp turn.
One rollover wrecks Ladder One（The bright-red fire engine rolled and wrecked, ladder bent, hoses scattered—a wreck that can no longer respond）; the ladder bends, hoses scatter.
In the hall, Huo Yan lunges to the positive-pressure respirator and clamps the half-detached supply hose.
The day after the flashover, Huo Yan stands in the company training hall, staring at the cracked positive-pressure respirator.
Huo Yan runs a finger along the facepiece crack, face dark.
On a sticky note beside the training log, Huo Yan records the date Ladder One rolled.
An old photo of Ladder One hangs on the hall wall; Huo Yan gazes a long time.
Huo Yan takes one of the five helmet lamps from the wall and sits alone by its faint light.
The damaged positive-pressure respirator still stands on the rack with its crack.
Weeks later, Huo Yan brings repair tools and begins fixing the positive-pressure respirator.

From a wooden crate Huo Yan takes a spare respirator（A half-worn spare respirator shaped much like the positive-pressure respirator, but shorter cylinder and gray plastic facepiece frame）; it closely resembles the positive-pressure respirator, yet the cylinder is shorter.
Huo Yan carefully replaces the facepiece and hose and stamps a maintenance mark.

The final airtight test passes; the positive-pressure respirator（After a new facepiece and hose, the positive-pressure respirator is airtight again; a maintenance stamp on the cylinder marks it apart from the first intact state） enters its replaced-repaired state.
The repaired positive-pressure respirator is ready to be worn on standby; Huo Yan watches it with relief.

A milky-white Foam Two（A brand-new milky-white foam fire engine, 'Foam Two' sprayed on the door, no aerial structure—utterly unlike Ladder One） rolls onto the wet asphalt drill yard, nothing like the wrecked Ladder One.

Supervisor Captain Shi Feng（Supervisor Captain Shi Feng in his forties, buzz cut, deep-blue drill uniform close to Huo Yan's build, but silver supervisor insignia on the shoulder） walks onto the yard and talks beside Huo Yan; the two are similar in build.
Shi Feng points at Foam Two, explaining the new response roster to Huo Yan.
Foam Two sounds its horn and leaves; Huo Yan alone on the yard watches it go.
Wind flaps the roster sheet Shi Feng left behind.

From outside the compound comes logistics recruit Xiaowei（Logistics recruit Xiaowei, seventeen or eighteen, orange-red helmet; at a glance like young Zhuqing, but no 'Qing' arm patch on the left arm, shy gaze） in an orange-red helmet; at a glance he somewhat resembles young Zhuqing.
Xiaowei practices coiling hose; Huo Yan shakes his head—he is not Zhuqing after all.
Xiaowei leaves the wet asphalt drill yard with an empty hose, back fading down the compound road.

Years later at dusk, Huo Yan（The same Huo Yan after burns: fresh bandage on the neck, left-leg splint, walking slowly on a metal crutch, still in that soot-stained deep-blue drill uniform） with a neck bandage leans on a metal crutch outside the company training hall.
Huo Yan leans on his crutch and looks up at the drill tower, gaze far away.
Those two assembly brass bells in the porch toll low in the wind; Huo Yan pauses with his crutch to listen.
Huo Yan lays a crutch-steady palm on the hall's cold concrete wall, as if saying goodbye.
He slowly sits on the yard's stone steps, splinted leg stretched straight.

By day, adult Zhuqing（Adult Zhuqing: a tall upright firefighter around twenty-three or twenty-four, still in orange-red helmet with cyan 'Qing' arm patch on the left arm, calm bearing） returns along the compound road and hurries toward the company training hall.
Outside the hall Zhuqing reunites with crutch-leaning Huo Yan; the two embrace.
Beside the medic-room narrow bed, Zhuqing holds Huo Yan's hand—old burn scar, now ice-cold.
Huo Yan（Huo Yan has closed his eyes in death, lying still on a narrow bed in the medic room, face peaceful, no breath left）'s breath fades; at last he closes his eyes and passes away.
Zhuqing gently sets Huo Yan's radio back by the pillow.
Huo Yan's deep-blue drill uniform still hangs behind the hall door; Zhuqing reaches out and gently strokes it.

By the drill-tower base, adult Zhuqing stands before a newly nailed merit plaque（A merit plaque nailed to the drill-tower base, engraved with Huo Yan's name and citation year, mottled verdigris at the edges）.
Zhuqing's fingertips brush Huo Yan's name engraved on the merit plaque.
Wind rises; assembly brass bells toll low in the distance; Zhuqing lifts her head.

Adult A-Qiao（Adult A-Qiao: nearly identical in face to adult Zhuqing, still in lemon-yellow helmet with rappel badge, publicity camera on the shoulder） comes from publicity and embraces Zhuqing tightly beneath the drill tower.
Zhuqing and A-Qiao stand side by side by the base—one calm, one bold.
They look at each other without words, at faces alike yet different.
A-Qiao raises the publicity camera, then silently lowers it, and simply stands with Zhuqing.
The shot returns to years ago—the youth touching a helmet reflection on wet asphalt appears again.
The opening moment returns—in the hall, a matte-black respirator completes its airtight test for the first time.
Flash back to that year's gear-bay corridor—a figure in a lemon-yellow helmet with a rappel badge flashes by.
Before the eyes again: that row of five old rechargeable helmet lamps on the east wall.
Back to the gleaming wet asphalt ground of first meeting; the drill tower stands tall, as it always did.
Zhuqing opens that water-stained training log again and walks into the company training hall.
By the hose rack, those three hose dividers are still lined up neat.
Zhuqing takes over the watch of the positive-pressure respirator; the cylinder valve is tightened for standby again.
Outside the hall door, wet-asphalt glare sharpens in the morning light.
